newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian govt 6-yr paper cut-off seen below 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian govt 6-yr paper cut-off seen below 12 pct.

text.p: A six-year government paper to be auctioned on Wednesday is expected to be at a yield of 11.90/95 percent, according to a poll of banks and debt researchers.
"There is too much liquidity in the system," said a money market dealer at a foreign bank.

A primary dealer in securities said he expected a cut-off of 11.85-11.90 percent. Another primary dealer said six-year papers are now quoted at 11.90-11.95 percent in the secondary market. "So you can expect the new issue at 11.95-12.0 percent."
Dealers at one of India's leading state-run banks endorsed this, saying 11.95 percent to 12.0 percent was a safe bet.
All the dealers Reuters spoke to were unanimous that the RBI would have no problem raising the targeted 30 billion rupees.
The manager (fixed income) at the Indian affiliate of a U.S. investment bank said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to fix a cut-off of 11.89 to 11.95 at the Wednesday auction.
"There is enough demand at these levels," he said.
A dealer at an American bank in Bombay said the subscriptions at recent RBI auctions was proof of the excess liquidity seeking investment avenues.
The RBI raised 62.50 billion rupees at a four-day repo auction on Tuesday at a cut-off rate of 3.60 percent.
"Despite such a large subscription, the call rates are easy at 1.5 percent level," the dealer said.
Earlier on July 11, the central bank raised 16.71 billion rupees at a 14-day treasury bill auction.
